lesson.title: Narrative Intelligence Framework
lesson.summary: Teach reviewers to understand the story before evaluating any individual sentence, including cross-scene meaning, scene purpose, character arc, relationship evolution, and story resolution.
learningObjectives: Separate narrator, character, and viewer interpretation.
Recognize symbolism, subtext, hidden meaning, and narrative context.
Track scene purpose, character arc, relationship evolution, and story resolution.
Use later context to revise early conclusions.

concepts.title: Story Arc
concepts.summary: Overall story progression from setup to resolution, used to understand the story before judging individual lines.

concepts.title: Story Goal
concepts.summary: The objective driving the story forward.

concepts.title: Story Conflict
concepts.summary: The central pressure or opposition in the story.

concepts.title: Story Resolution
concepts.summary: The ending phase that resolves or transforms the conflict and can reframe earlier scenes.

concepts.title: Story Progression
concepts.summary: The ordered movement of events across the narrative.

concepts.title: Scene Goal
concepts.summary: The purpose of a scene at the local level; the scene purpose the reviewer should recover before judging it.

concepts.title: Scene Transition
concepts.summary: A shift between scenes, beats, or locations.

concepts.title: Character Arc
concepts.summary: A character's evolution across the story, including motivation, belief, and moral change.

concepts.title: Relationship Arc
concepts.summary: The changing bond between characters over time; the relationship evolution the reviewer tracks across scenes.

concepts.title: Motivation Change
concepts.summary: A shift in what a character wants or why they act.

concepts.title: Belief Change
concepts.summary: A shift in what a character believes to be true.

concepts.title: Moral Change
concepts.summary: A shift in a character's ethical stance.

concepts.title: Tone Shift
concepts.summary: A noticeable change in emotional or stylistic tone.

concepts.title: Theme
concepts.summary: The central idea or message of the story.

concepts.title: Subtext
concepts.summary: Meaning implied beneath the literal wording.

concepts.title: Hidden Meaning
concepts.summary: Meaning revealed by context rather than explicit wording.

concepts.title: Symbolism
concepts.summary: Objects or actions that stand for deeper meaning.

concepts.title: Foreshadowing
concepts.summary: An earlier clue that points toward a later event.

concepts.title: Callback
concepts.summary: A later reference to an earlier detail.

concepts.title: Plot Twist
concepts.summary: A surprising change that reinterprets previous events.

concepts.title: Red Herring
concepts.summary: A misleading clue that pulls attention away from the real meaning.

concepts.title: Flashback
concepts.summary: A return to an earlier event in time.

concepts.title: Flashforward
concepts.summary: A preview of a later event or outcome.

concepts.title: Dream
concepts.summary: A scene framed as a dream or dreamlike experience.

concepts.title: Hallucination
concepts.summary: A scene framed as perception that may not be real.

concepts.title: Imaginary Sequence
concepts.summary: A sequence that exists only in a character's mind.

concepts.title: Voice Over
concepts.summary: Narration spoken over the visual scene.

concepts.title: Unreliable Narrator
concepts.summary: A narrator whose account may not be trustworthy.

concepts.title: Parallel Story
concepts.summary: A second story line that mirrors or contrasts the first.

concepts.title: Background Story
concepts.summary: Events that happened before the current scene.

concepts.title: Scene Description
concepts.summary: Visual or written description of what is happening.

concepts.title: Environmental Storytelling
concepts.summary: Meaning conveyed through objects, space, or setting.

concepts.title: Off Screen Event
concepts.summary: An event that happens outside the visible scene.

concepts.title: Implicit Event
concepts.summary: An event inferred from context rather than directly shown.

concepts.title: Missing Information
concepts.summary: A gap that prevents a full conclusion.

concepts.title: Time Skip
concepts.summary: A jump forward or backward in time.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: What is the story doing overall?
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Start with the full scene before judging a sentence.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must cite story-level evidence.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Separate character speech from narrator voice.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Who or what is the target of the scene?
evidenceRequirements: The answer must mention the target clue.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Decide whether the scene is endorsement, criticism, neutral narration, or fiction.
Track flashback, dream, voice over, and unreliable narration.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must point to context evidence.
The answer must use scene evidence.

reviewerQuestions.purpose: Does earlier or later memory change the reading?
reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Cross-scene context can reverse a first impression.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must cite the relevant scene or sentence.

reviewerQuestions.reasoningGuidance: Confidence should fall when context is incomplete.
evidenceRequirements: The answer must reflect evidence strength.

examples: A single line can appear harmless until the next scene reveals the real meaning.
A dream sequence should not be read as literal story reality.
A narrator's opinion is not always the author's opinion.
counterExamples: Treating one sentence as the whole story.
Ignoring later scenes that change the interpretation.
Confusing a character's opinion with the story's opinion.

minimum: The scene must include at least one literal narrative clue.
A sentence alone is not enough when later context changes the meaning.
strong: Dialogue plus action plus later scene context.
Narration that explicitly frames the story meaning.
A recurring motif that is confirmed in a later scene.
weak: One isolated sentence without narrative support.
A symbol with no supporting scene context.
A claim about meaning without an actual story clue.
insufficient: Guessing author intent from a single line.
Assuming the narrator and the author are the same voice.
confidenceGuidance: High confidence requires corroboration across more than one scene or signal.
Medium confidence is appropriate when a strong clue exists but later reversal remains possible.
Low confidence is appropriate when the scene is isolated or ambiguous.
Review is appropriate when narration, symbolism, or memory materially changes the reading.

glossaryReferences.note: Story is the primary unit of analysis.
Symbolism often points beyond the literal line.
